theme: Dated continuity evidence between Indus marks and early historic South Asian scripts
question: How far does the dated South Asian mark/writing record reach backwards from early historic scripts toward late Indus material, where does the recovered chain break, and which observations discriminate transmission from convergence?
outcome: 42 documentary rows, 18 sources, 11 attributed claims and 33 century bins. Nineteen dated additive rows: 2 A, 9 B, 8 C. All A+B brackets leave two one-century internal gaps; the high/moderate calendar-strength subset has a six-bin internal gap from 1300 to 700 BCE. No recovered dated diagnostic chain establishes late Indus-to-early historic transmission. Coverage arithmetic is Verified computation; archaeological assessments remain Exploratory; four tests are Proposed.
challenge: Legacy absolute chronologies, uncalibrated labels, site-wide counts lacking layer allocation, pooled populations and incomplete sample/specimen joins. Nine direct downloads failed or were blocked; primary Bactrian pages and full Anuradhapura article remained unavailable. Early search strings were not retained exactly.
remedy: Separate dating methods, specimen links and calendar strength; retain missing target rows; exclude pooled/unaligned/site-unit totals; preserve raw witnesses locally; reproduce calculations in fresh directories; specify rare-feature, shape-null, seriation and positional tests with acquisition thresholds.
retry_when: Recover original Porunthal calibration outputs and marked grave register; full Anuradhapura sample/specimen tables; calibrated legacy Gujarat/Deccan mark contexts; primary OCP/Copper Hoard/PGW/NBPW marked inventories; or a dated individual-object Tamil Nadu sequence. Freeze matching rules and complexity/context controls before testing. Existing resemblance/stroke outputs alone do not justify rerunning a transmission claim.
